basis: Congenital intrahepatic portosystemic shunt diverts portal blood away from hepatic perfusion; common persistent neurologic damage is not established.

decisions.hepatic: primary: the intrahepatic shunt and diversion of hepatic portal perfusion define this congenital liver vascular anomaly.

basis: Muscular dystrophy caused by an inherited dystroglycan glycosylation disorder; borderline intellectual disability in 2/2 patients supports neurologic involvement.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: established defective alpha-dystroglycan O-glycosylation is an inborn metabolic disorder, supported by the disease ancestry.

basis: Cardiac and skeletal abnormalities characterize this umbrella; intellectual disability affects ~6-23% in typical Noonan syndrome, with higher rates in selected related syndromes.

decisions.neurologic: none: persistent neurologic impairment is not established in ≥30% across this umbrella; intellectual disability in typical Noonan syndrome is ~6-23%.

basis: Bulbar and spinal motor-neuron degeneration causes progressive denervation, muscle atrophy and loss of skeletal-muscle function in most patients.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: progressive denervation causes actual muscle atrophy and loss of function in most patients; muscle injury need not be primary myopathy.

basis: Odontogenic epithelial neoplasm usually arising within mandibular or maxillary bone; tooth-forming tissue and intraosseous jaw location define its origin.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: approximately 95% arise as intraosseous jaw tumors; bone is the primary anatomical site, rather than merely a site of secondary invasion.

basis: Developmental impairment characterizes the syndrome; cleft palate and pharyngeal abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. Cardiac, renal, hearing and immune defects are occasional.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate directly affects oral structure in 30-79%; it is a common associated malformation rather than a defining diagnostic requirement.

basis: Chronic maxillary sinus inflammation defines the disease; mixed infectious, allergic and structural causes do not establish a uniform infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: infection and allergy are possible causes, but this umbrella also includes structural causes; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.

basis: Severe congenital long-QT syndrome defines cardiac disease; developmental neurologic impairment was reported in roughly half of early atypical Timothy cases.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental neurologic impairment occurs in approximately half of early reported atypical Timothy cases, supporting the ≥30% threshold.

basis: Recurrent subcutaneous and submucosal angioedema defines the disease; intestinal and laryngeal edema each occur in 30-79%. Bradykinin excess does not establish immune disease.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: recurrent upper-airway mucosal edema is a defining manifestation, with laryngeal edema reported in 30-79%.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: recurrent intestinal mucosal edema is a defining manifestation, reported in 30-79%; it is the disease itself rather than a secondary complication.

basis: Recrudescent Rickettsia prowazekii infection targets vascular endothelium and produces small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash adds no skin axis.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection and small-vessel vasculitis are the disease's characteristic tissue pathology, rather than a minority cardiac complication.
